simple: Where you put a script in the Explorer changes whether it runs, and where it runs: on the server or on a player's device. This page explains the three kinds of scripts and the `RunContext` setting. It also gives Roblox's advice for organizing code, using ModuleScripts for most of it. Getting this right saves you from the classic 'why is my script not running?' problem.
analogy: It is like a school: some notes are for the principal's office only (server), some are for each student's desk (client), and some go on the shared bulletin board everyone can read (ReplicatedStorage). Put a note in the wrong place and the right person never reads it.
keyPoints: There are three script types: `Script` (server or client, depending on `RunContext`), `LocalScript` (client only), and `ModuleScript` (reusable code other scripts load).
A new `Script` has `RunContext = Legacy`, so it runs on the server and only from server places like ServerScriptService or Workspace.
Setting `RunContext` to `Client` lets a `Script` run on the player's device from ReplicatedStorage.
Do not put Client-run Scripts in Starter folders; they get copied, so both the original and the copy run.
Recommended setup: one Server script in ServerScriptService, one Client script in ReplicatedStorage, and most code in ModuleScripts they `require`.
Give each ModuleScript a `start()` function, so all modules load first and then start together.
Use LocalScripts sparingly, and only in StarterPlayerScripts, StarterCharacterScripts, StarterGui, or StarterPack.
Instead of putting scripts inside Workspace objects, tag the objects and handle them with `CollectionService` from one module.

terms.server: Roblox's computer that runs the game for everyone. It is in charge of the real game state.
terms.client: One player's own device, like their PC, phone, or console.
terms.RunContext: A setting on a `Script` that decides if it runs as Legacy, Server, or Client.
terms.container: A folder-like service in the Explorer, such as ServerScriptService or ReplicatedStorage.
terms.replicate: Copy from the server to players' devices. Things in ReplicatedStorage are copied to every client.
terms.ServerScriptService: A container for server scripts. Players' devices cannot see what is inside.
terms.ServerStorage: A server-only storage area. Scripts do not run there, but you can keep ModuleScripts and big objects there.
terms.ReplicatedFirst: A container copied to players before anything else, used for loading screens.
terms.Starter containers: StarterPlayerScripts, StarterCharacterScripts, StarterGui, and StarterPack. Their contents are copied into each player when they join or spawn.
terms.require: A function that loads a ModuleScript and gives back what it returns.
terms.entry point: The one place where your code starts running.
terms.tag: A label you put on objects, like "npc", so a script can find all of them.
terms.CollectionService: A service that finds all objects with a certain tag and tells you when tagged objects are added or removed.
terms.ephemeral: Temporary. A copied script's location only exists while the game runs.

example.title: One server script that starts a module
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService, plus a ModuleScript named Greeter in ServerScriptService
example.code:
-- ModuleScript named "Greeter" (in ServerScriptService)
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local Greeter = {}

function Greeter.start()
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
		print("Welcome, " .. player.Name .. "!")
	end)
end

return Greeter

-- Script (in ServerScriptService) - put this part in a separate Script
--[[
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local Greeter = require(ServerScriptService.Greeter)

Greeter.start()
]]
explain: The ModuleScript builds a table called `Greeter` and adds a `start()` function to it.
`start()` sets up the code that greets each player who joins.
The module ends with `return Greeter` so other scripts can use it.
The separate Script (shown in the comment) loads the module with `require` and calls `Greeter.start()`.
This way your server has one entry point, and adding more features is just adding more modules.

watchOut: A LocalScript in ReplicatedStorage or Workspace will not run. Put it in a Starter container, or use a Script with `RunContext = Client` in ReplicatedStorage.
Server scripts in ReplicatedStorage can be seen by players' devices. Keep server code in ServerScriptService.
Scripts in ServerStorage never run. Only ModuleScripts that are required from somewhere else are useful there.
Setting `RunContext = Client` on a script inside a Starter folder makes it run twice.
